key_insight: Repurposes large language models to perform non‑visual 4D reconstruction from everyday wearable IMUs, recovering human motion and 3D scene layout without cameras.
problem_solved: Reduces reliance on cameras for human activity and environment understanding, addressing persistent privacy, safety, energy, and scalability challenges by using inertial wearable sensors instead of vision.
method: Use streams from everyday wearable IMUs as the sole input modality and encode spatiotemporal inertial signals.
Repurpose large language models as spatiotemporal reasoning modules to map IMU sequences to scene-aware predictions.
Decode outputs into a 4D representation: time-varying 3D human pose together with reconstructed scene geometry/layout for downstream tasks.
impact: Offers a privacy-preserving, low-power alternative for 4D perception useful in AR/VR, healthcare monitoring, and robotics, and highlights a novel role for LLMs beyond text as general spatiotemporal reasoners—opening new research directions and deployment options.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: wearable IMUs on a person → LLM-based reasoning block → 4D output (animated 3D human + scene layout).
Side-by-side comparison chart: camera-based vs IMU-based sensing (privacy, energy, robustness, scalability).
Sequence of 3D frames (time-lapse) showing reconstructed human motion inside inferred scene geometry.
Icon set: wearable sensor, LLM/brain, privacy shield, low-power/battery to emphasize benefits.
paper_title: Seeing Without Eyes: 4D Human-Scene Understanding from Wearable IMUs
paper_authors: Hao-Yu Hsu, Tianhang Cheng, Jing Wen, Alexander G. Schwing, Shenlong Wang
